question: Who is a holder in due course under the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881? Explain the privileges available to a holder in due course.
sources: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, Section 9 (holder in due course) and provisions on the privileges of a holder in due course

points.label: Definition
points.description: A holder in due course is a person who, for consideration, became the possessor (if payable to bearer) or the payee or indorsee (if payable to order) of a negotiable instrument before the amount became payable.

points.label: Good faith
points.description: He must have taken the instrument without having sufficient cause to believe that any defect existed in the title of the person from whom he got it.

points.label: Better title free from defects
points.description: A holder in due course gets a good title free from defects in the title of prior parties, and every prior party remains liable to him until the instrument is duly satisfied.
points.basis: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, privileges of a holder in due course

points.label: Title passes to later holders
points.description: A person who takes from a holder in due course gets the same rights as that holder in due course, even if not one himself, provided he was not party to any fraud affecting the instrument.
points.basis: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, rights of a holder deriving title from a holder in due course

points.label: Estoppel and presumption
points.description: Parties such as the maker, drawer and acceptor cannot deny the original validity of the instrument against a holder in due course, and every holder is presumed to be a holder in due course until the contrary is proved.
points.basis: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, estoppel against denying original validity and presumptions as to negotiable instruments
